answers.rationale: Marisol repeatedly favors a nearby breakfast-included limited-service hotel when the event venue is still an easy walk and there is no stated same-building early-morning requirement. Hampton is only $5 less but has clearly included breakfast and is the only leading option that does not infer that breakfast is covered merely because the Seelbach offers a buffet. The Seelbach buffet should remain paid or unverified until confirmed as part of the block rate.

Fairfield preserves a short no-car commute for the 8:15 starts while providing an explicitly included breakfast at a slightly lower rate. The Davenport wording establishes that breakfast is served onsite, not that it is included in the block. Marisol has accepted a short walk or ride to save meaningful lodging-and-breakfast cost when the event hotel is not required for the morning agenda.

SpringHill is the most practical balance for an evening arrival and 8:30 downtown sessions: it has an actual listed in-room coffeemaker and mini-fridge, remains close to the sessions, and has nearby casual dinner choices. The boutique option lacks confirmed refrigeration, the Hyatt only offers refrigeration by request and gains only one reception attachment, and Homewood costs more while requiring a longer ride and offering weaker dinner access.

Campus Hampton best fits the early campus start and no-car plan while clearly listing the useful room basics: in-room coffee and a mini-fridge. The slightly closer boutique room substitutes lobby coffee and has no confirmed refrigerator; Marriott makes the fridge request-only; and Residence Inn's lower rate does not outweigh the much longer morning ride and irrelevant free parking.
